title: E0050: Position check used as boolean
plain_english: `strpos()`, `stripos()`, `strrpos()`, and `strripos()` return `0` when the match is at the very start of the string. In a boolean context, PHP treats `0` as false, so a condition like `if (strpos(...))` treats a match at position zero as "not found."
why_matters: A valid match at the beginning of the string can silently take the wrong branch, causing incorrect behavior that is easy to miss in testing.
what_it_checks: Checks used as a ternary condition
